title: Regulatory Architecture of GM12878 Promoters: Quantitative Analysis of the Relationship Between TFBS, Chromatin Accessibility, and Expression
content: Introduction. Chromatin accessibility at promoters is determined by a combination of factors: nucleotide composition, transcription factor (TF) binding, and 3D genome architecture. The quantitative contribution of each of these components remains a subject of debate.Results. We integrated ChIP-seq for 122 transcription factors, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq for 7,886 promoters of the GM12878 cell line. TF binding profiles distinguish promoters with ATAC signal above and below the median with ROC-AUC = 0.880, significantly outperforming a model based on GC content (0.611). IKZF1 showed one of the strongest univariate correlations with ATAC (ρ = 0.589), comparable to ELF1 (0.633), ZNF143 (0.615), and BHLHE40 (0.610), and a pronounced deviation from unimodality (dip test: dip = 0.166, p < 10⁻¹⁶; rank 29 of 118 factors by dip statistic), whereas no significant deviation from unimodality was detected for ATAC signal (dip = 0.005, p = 0.244). This indicates that the unimodality hypothesis is rejected for TF occupancy but not for chromatin accessibility. Hyperbolic embedding (Poincaré ball) provides an interpretable visualization of the hierarchy of TFBS profiles; however, the core/periphery structure is also recovered by linear PCA (ARI = 0.56–0.60), indicating predominantly linear separability of the main axis. Cluster analysis identifies two extreme groups of promoters: a "generic" core (n = 2563) with low TF occupancy, accessibility, and expression, and a specialized periphery (n = 5323) with high values, while bootstrap analysis (ARI = 0.573, 95% CI: 0.515–0.628) indicates moderate stability of the boundary between them, consistent with a continuum organization with two pronounced extreme states rather than two discrete modes. The partition is also robust to normalization (mean ARI = 0.625) and to removal of individual factors (ARI = 0.593). K-means in the tangent space at the origin gives ARI = 0.988 relative to the reference, indicating no effect of the geometric inconsistency of the original method on the results in our data regime (‖h‖max = 0.314 ≪ 1). Mediation analysis shows that, within the chosen statistical model, RNA mediates only ~2.7% of the IKZF1–ATAC association, suggesting a predominantly direct influence of IKZF1 on chromatin accessibility. This signal, however, is shared with several other active-promoter factors and is therefore not specific to IKZF1.Conclusions. Our results form a testable hypothesis about the involvement of IKZF1-associated regulatory programs in organizing accessible promoter chromatin and demonstrate a substantial dependence of conclusions on the spatial resolution of analysis.
